items.title: Glenn Zottola interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 7, 2020
items.q: you know what I mean? He said, “I’ve been listening to you, you’ve been listening to Pops.”

ctx.x: Wow. That is not the typical Benny story.

That is not — you mention Benny’s name in a crowd you know you get an hour’s worth, right? Now the other story is Count Basie. I did the warm-up act for Basie and I’m coming off stage and I’m walking past his dressing room, never met him, and I hear this voice, “Young man, young man, come in here.” I go in and there’s Count Basie. Now people don’t realize that in Newark that’s like walking in on Elvis or Michael Jackson, you know what I mean? He said, “I’ve been listening to you, you’ve been listening to Pops.” I…
there, oh my God. Count Basie takes time out of his life to call this white kid into his dressing room to validate his playing. Unbelievable. You know.
